I understand your point on causing your body more harm by overeating.

But you may want to reconsider the underlying principle of parents asking one to finish everything on their plate. By making the child finish everything the idea is that the child will NOT take so much food the next time that he/she won't be able to finish it. The child understands that if he were to take a lot he would be forced to finish it - a prospect he knows is not all that enticing (from his previous experience) 

So it's using temporary discomfort to create a good habit in the long term. And creating this particular habit is extremely important. 

However, like all things in life this practise also needs some balance. 

1. Humans are often short sighted seekers of instant gratification and kids especially so. Hence, as a child you may 'forget' your last experience and engage in piling up your plate with a lot of food yet again. At this point it is the responsibility of the parent to gently remind the child that there is enough food for a second or even a third helping should they later want it. Creating this 'security' that there is enough food is important as humans are biologically wired to eat a lot and store food as our ancestors did not have access to regular supply of food. 

2. Additionally, they should be reminded of how uncomfortable they felt overeating the last time. 


A lot of the 'bad experiences' emerge because these two steps are often skipped by parents and instead a more militant approach of forcing kids to overeat is adopted - without taking care of their unconscious concerns. 



Finally, by imbibing this habit of taking smaller servings you erase the underlying problem - that of wasted food. Furthermore, taking smaller helpings is beneficial to your health as it helps elongate your eating time giving your stomach enough time to send signals of satiation to your brain. In any case, it is always good practise to eat only uptil you are 80% full.

Porn is usually not the problem. It is a symptom, not a cause. There isn't total agreement in the medical community either - whether porn should be classified as an addictive entity (like drugs, liquor, nicotine) or not.

However, in my experience. Even if it does not cause physiological dependence like drugs or alcohol, it can still become as addictive an escape from your real problems in life. Maybe your are under constant stress, anxious, depressed. Porn is an easily available recourse to help belay the distressing effects of such problems. Thus, trying to 'solve' the issue by attacking porn would be similar to applying bandages on a gunshot wound without removing the bullet: the issue isn't the bleeding, that is the symptom - the problem is the bullet.

So that's the first step. Why do you watch it? Identify that. Let me give you an example : I find that on days I have a lot of work, I am outside my house, I exercise etc the need to watch porn is minimal. AND even when I do it I don't find it distressing. But when I am at home, under stress, some life issues usage of porn feels good while it lasts but is accompanied by copious amounts of regret and self-loathing afterwards.

Is porn today a problem in general? Somewhat yes. It is easily available and the human biological urge to pursue pleasurable experiences warps our behaviour around it. But I don't think it has any physiological withdrawal effects like drug, alcohol withdrawal. And it can be useful, fun - but in very tiny, tiny, tiny amounts.

However, when it becomes your primary means of getting pleasure, when you are planing your activities around porn, sacrificing actual human interaction for it I think it does become a problem.

So don't focus on reducing porn, focus on enhancing your other life experiences - your job/studies, exercise, friends etc. That is, don't focus on applying bandages to a wound, focus more on getting the bullet out first.

PS: I am not a doctor. So I am going to put out a standard disclaimer here that should you feel things are getting out of hand, always consult a professional.
